case_notes: Tests an allegation that is investigated but never resolved within the available sources: no admission, no conviction, no clearance, and no timeline for when the matter will be resolved. Unlike the earlier conflicting-sources case (which included an exculpatory audit), this case deliberately withholds any resolution, since in this project negative sentiment functions as a review flag rather than a finding of guilt, an open, unresolved investigation should still produce an overall negative result. A prior-record source is included specifically to confirm that a single unresolved allegation still outweighs an otherwise strong track record.
expected_failure_modes: may treat the allegation as neutral because guilt was never established
may soften or drop the flag in the final justification because there is no confirmed outcome
may overstate the allegation as confirmed wrongdoing rather than an open investigation
may let the positive prior-record source outweigh the unresolved allegation

sources.title: City Opens Investigation Into Travel Reimbursements Filed by Samantha Reeves
sources.article_text:
The city comptroller's office has opened a formal investigation into travel reimbursement requests filed by Samantha Reeves, deputy director of the parks and recreation department, after an internal audit flagged a pattern of expense claims that could not be matched to corresponding travel records. The audit, part of a routine review of department spending, identified roughly $9,000 in reimbursements submitted over the past two years that auditors said lacked adequate supporting documentation.

Comptroller's office spokesperson Daniel Ruiz said the review is still in its early stages and cautioned that flagged discrepancies do not necessarily indicate wrongdoing. 'An audit finding is the start of a process, not a conclusion,' Ruiz said. 'We follow up on every discrepancy above a certain threshold as a matter of routine.'

Reeves has been placed on paid administrative leave while the investigation proceeds, a standard step the city said it takes whenever a department official is the subject of an active financial review. Reeves has not been charged with any offense. Through an attorney, Reeves said she disputes the audit's characterization of her expense filings and looks forward to providing documentation she says will resolve the matter.

The parks and recreation department said it could not comment further while the investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: Investigation Into Reeves' Travel Expenses Still Open, City Says
sources.article_text:
Six weeks after the city comptroller's office opened a review of travel reimbursements filed by parks and recreation deputy director Samantha Reeves, the investigation remains open with no timeline for completion, officials said Tuesday. Comptroller's office spokesperson Daniel Ruiz said the review has expanded slightly to include a broader sample of department expense filings from the same period, but declined to say whether any additional discrepancies had been found.

Reeves remains on paid administrative leave and has not been charged with any offense. Her attorney, Marcus Webb, said Reeves has submitted additional receipts and calendar records to the comptroller's office and maintains that the missing documentation reflects a recordkeeping gap rather than any improper claim. 'Ms. Reeves has cooperated fully with every request from the comptroller's office, and we expect this to be resolved once they've had a chance to review what we've submitted,' Webb said.

City council member Elena Garcia said she had asked the comptroller's office for a status update and was told only that the matter remained under active review. No hearing date has been set.

sources.title: Parks Department Names Samantha Reeves 2025 Employee of the Year
sources.article_text:
The parks and recreation department named deputy director Samantha Reeves its 2025 Employee of the Year at last December's staff recognition dinner, citing her work expanding the department's after-school sports programming to five additional neighborhoods. Reeves, who has worked for the department for nine years, was credited with securing a state grant that funded new equipment for three community centers.

Department director Thomas Lee said at the time that Reeves' organizational skills and attention to detail had made her one of the most reliable members of his leadership team. Colleagues described her as detail-oriented and responsive, frequently the first to catch scheduling conflicts before they became problems for program participants.

Reeves said she was honored by the recognition and credited her staff for the programming expansion's success.
